title: A Look At An Emerging Runtime Enforcement Layer For Agents - Hooks
snippet: Surveys the before-tool-call hook pattern now shipping in production runtimes: OpenClaw's before_tool_call plugin, Cursor's beforeShellExecution, Claude Code's PreToolUse hook, and LangChain's on_tool_start callback, each gating execution on an external policy decision.

title: Agent Hooks: An open, framework-neutral AI governance contract
snippet: Microsoft proposes Agent Hooks, a framework-neutral contract that lets a governance or authorization component intercept an agent's proposed tool call before execution and return an allow/deny decision, independent of the underlying agent framework.

title: From Logic Monopoly to Social Contract: Separation of Power and the Institutional Foundations for Autonomous Agent Economies
snippet: Notes Coinbase launched the first wallet infrastructure explicitly designed for AI agents in February 2026, featuring programmable guardrails (session caps, transaction limits, operation allowlists), multi-party approvals, and detailed audit logs. Discusses ERC-1812 verifiable claims enabling signed attestations that policy engines can check on identity, entitlements, or constraints before a payment is authorized.

title: draft-schrock-ep-authorization-receipts-12 - Authorization Receipts for High-Risk Agent Actions
snippet: Adjacent IETF Internet-Draft defining authorization receipts for high-risk AI agent actions. Describes mandate binding self-declared by the issuer, scoped to a set of authorized action types, with verifiers resolving scope_digest by retrieving the mandate via mandate_id and recomputing the digest over canonical scope bytes; mismatch is a non-conformance condition. Competing/complementary work in the same agent-authorization receipt space as @bolyra/receipts and @bolyra/mpp.
